# Discussion

## Limitations of the study

Although for the experiment that took place in 2023 different species were used, only limited valve data was available due to an issue of data be overwritten. Therefore its use to assess the functioning of the fish spiral was limited. During the first experiment of 2024 this issue was resolved, though it seemed that the temporal resolution of the valve data was too low to capture the moment the valves opened and closed. The last two experiments had sound valve measurement data for the entire duration of the experiment at an adequate temporal resolution.

## Insights gained

The cycle duration and phase distribution of exp0 (2023) were completely different from the experiments of 2024. For exp0, cycle duration was twice as long and phase distribution was much more comparable between the lower and upper valve. For the experiments of 2024 (exp1 to exp3) the cycle duration and phase distribution can be considered the same, though this was not apparent from the data because of the too low temporal resolution of the exp1 valve-opening data. In contrast with the experiment of 2023, for the experiments of 2024 the lower valve was closed most of the time, while the upper valve was open most of the time.

Despite the same operational settings of the fish spiral throughout the experiments of 2024, **passage success varied substantially** as it ranged **between 0.47 and 0.79**. It is very difficult to determine the underlying cause behind this difference as these passage success values are not exact values but underestimations and local, potentially interfering, conditions might have been present but were only sporadically measured (e.g. water quality). In addition, fish were re-used for the different experiments and their familiarity with the system might have had an effect (though the available results do not indicate any effect). **The length, weight and species did not have any effect on whether fish were able to successfully use the fish spiral, nor did it have an effect on the time it took fish to move up the fish spiral.**

Fish generally **wait until the valves are completely open before entering and leaving the fish spiral,** though for the upper valve a relatively large amount of fish also seem to leave the fish spiral when the valve is opening or closing.
